race_context: The district: the ballot's 'Delaware Liberty Perry' offices are seats on the board of Liberty-Perry Community School Corporation in Delaware County, whose board seats are listed by county election officials as Liberty Township, Perry Township and at-large {dc_2022}{sp_2022_filing}. The district operates Selma Elementary, Selma Middle School and Wapahani High School near Selma {mj_playground}{wiki_wapahani}. Aaron Black is superintendent {mj_playground}. Wikipedia lists Wapahani High School enrollment at 334 in 2023–24 {wiki_wapahani}; this guide did not find a verified district-wide enrollment figure.

How the board is elected: county results show three Liberty-Perry seats on the 2022 ballot (Liberty Township, Perry Township and at-large) and two on the 2024 ballot (Liberty Township and Perry Township), each 'vote for 1' {dc_2022}{dc_2024}. That pattern points to a five-member board with staggered four-year terms, but this guide could not open the district's website to confirm the board's size or current membership.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the three seats elected in 2022 are up, and each race elects one member, matching the state list {dc_2022}{in_list}. In 2022 Kevin Thomas won the at-large seat with 45.83% over Shane Sites and Eugene Ferris; Shane Wise won the Liberty Township seat with 41.63% over incumbent Keith Davis (32.83%) and Craig Standish (25.55%); and Robert Paul Cook was unopposed for Perry Township {dc_2022}{sp_2022_races}.

Who is running: Thomas is not on the 2026 candidate list, so the at-large seat is open and Dale Buffin, listed as a Republican, is the only candidate {in_list}{dc_2022}. In Liberty Township, Daniel Shane Wise faces Craig R Standish, a rematch of two of the 2022 candidates if, as appears likely, Daniel Shane Wise is the Shane Wise elected in 2022 {in_list}{dc_2022}. Robert Cook is unopposed for Perry Township {in_list}.
Party labels: under the 2025 law that lets school board candidates list a party, one candidate in this district is listed as a Republican and three as Nonpartisan {in_list}.

Facilities (August 2026): the district opened a wheelchair-accessible playground at Selma Elementary on Aug. 10, 2026; the project cost more than $187,000 and was funded by local government, foundation, business and PTO contributors {mj_playground}.
School safety (September 2026): Liberty-Perry Community School Corp. received a $49,880 state Secured School Safety Grant, according to a release from local state representatives {mj_safety}.

Issues not verified: this guide could not open Liberty-Perry board agendas, minutes or budget documents and found no 2025–2026 news coverage of the district's budget, the effect of the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1), referendums or other board decisions.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of this race.
